photos.title: Hurricane Florence - South Carolina National Guard Responds (44200296354)
photos.what: A street of single-story houses with floodwater across the road and the yards, a basketball hoop and road signs standing in the water, trees and a power pole reflected in the water, under a gray sky.
photos.caption: Floodwater on a street of houses in the Conway area after Florence.
photos.alt: Floodwater covering a residential street and the yards of single-story houses, with road signs standing in the water, in the Conway area after Hurricane Florence

place.sublocation: Conway area, South Carolina (the source does not name the street)

photos.author: Senior Master Sgt. Edward Snyder, 169th Fighter Wing, South Carolina National Guard
photos.credit: Photo: South Carolina National Guard (Senior Master Sgt. Edward Snyder), public domain, via Wikimedia Commons.
photos.provenance: U.S. National Guard photo, taken 2018-09-25 by Senior Master Sgt. Edward Snyder, 169th Fighter Wing public affairs, as part of his official duties. Uploaded to Flickr by the South Carolina National Guard (flickr.com/photos/scguard/44200296354, marked Public Domain) and to Wikimedia Commons with PD-USGov-Military-National_Guard; FlickreviewR passed. Commons description (shared by the set): 'Flood waters continue to rise in Conway, S.C., impacting surrounding cities and neighborhoods to include Myrtle Beach, S.C., Sept. 25, 2018.' Downloaded as the Commons 1920 px thumbnail on 2026-11-01. Checked by the batch verifier (VERIFY.md, photo P1).
photos.license_note: Commons: 'This image or file is a work of a U.S. Army National Guard or Air National Guard Soldier or Airman ... taken or made as part of that person's official duties. As a work of the U.S. federal government, the image or file is in the public domain.'
photos.subject_check: Looked at full size (1920 px) by the writer of /buyers/undisclosed-flooding/ on 2026-11-01: single-story houses, water over the road and yards, a basketball hoop, speed limit, no thru trucks and speed hump signs in the water. The source does not name the street, so the caption names only the Conway area. A mailbox number at the left edge was partly readable; the left 100 px were cropped off. No person, no readable house number or plate, no business sign.
